title: Loss of consciousness or seizure
summary: Unresponsive crew member, loss of consciousness, fainting or an observed seizure. Distinguish current loss of consciousness, a resolved episode and a seizure event. Criteria for immediate alert: unresponsive, first seizure, seizure lasting more than five minutes, repeated seizures without recovery, or difficulty breathing or waking up. After a faint with recovery, check whether cardiac signs, neurological signs or a blow to the head occurred at the same time. Informational support only: not a diagnosis or a treatment decision. There are no clinical personnel on board: the steps are first aid and monitoring; treatment depends on mission procedures.

notify: mission control (if the link is up)

steps.text: Check airway, breathing and pulse frequently; start CPR if needed.
If the person is breathing and you do not suspect a spinal injury, place them on their side (recovery position).
Do not leave the person alone, do not give them food or drink, and do not put a pillow under their head.

notify: mission control (if the link is up)

steps.text: Stay with the person and move away objects they could hit; do not hold them down or put anything in their mouth.
Time the seizure: more than 5 minutes, another seizure right after, difficulty breathing or waking up, or an injury require emergency help.
When it ends, place the person on their side in a safe place; do not give water or food until they are fully alert.
If it happened to you and you are alone: do not eat or drink until you are fully alert, and call for help.

fainted_recovered.text: Faint with recovery: lie down and check whether there were palpitations, chest pain, neurological signs or a blow to the head; if there were, treat it as an emergency.
notify: mission control (if the link is up)

steps.text: Lie down and, if you can, raise your feet about 30 cm to avoid another fall.
Another crew member: do not leave the person alone.

recovery_check.text: Faint reported without knowing whether the person has recovered: confirm their level of consciousness. If they do not respond, it is an emergency.
notify: mission control (if the link is up)

steps.text: Check whether the person responds; a sudden, unexplained change in mental status is an emergency.

questions.recovered: Has the person regained consciousness and are they responding normally?
